triggers.help: Triggers fire this flow automatically. Webhook triggers expose <0>POST /trigger/{{tenant}}/{{workspace}}/{{id}}</0> — callers send the per-graph secret as a bearer token. Cron triggers run on a workspace-local schedule.
triggers.empty: No triggers yet. Add one to fire this flow without a manual run.
triggers.bearerSecretDesc: Callers must send <0>Authorization: Bearer <this></0>. The value is stored plain in the graph file — for production consider rotating periodically.
triggers.curlDesc: The webhook listener runs on whatever address the daemon was started with via <0>--webhook</0> (off by default; we use <0>:8089</0> here). Replace the host with your public URL when calling from outside. The request body lands on the <0>webhook_input</0> node's <0>body</0> port: plain-text bodies arrive as a string (works directly with string-consuming drops like Slack send-message), JSON bodies arrive as a parsed object (use a transform drop to extract a field, or switch <0>Content-Type</0> to <0>application/json</0> with a JSON payload if downstream expects structure).
triggers.cronHelp: 5-field cron: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. Example: <0> 0 9 * * 1-5</0> = 09:00 weekdays.
triggers.dayOfMonthCaveat: Note: months without day {{day}} (e.g. February) will skip — the run won't fire that month.

recipes.title: How do I connect my website form?
recipes.intro: Your form needs to send each submission to the address below, with the header that proves it's allowed. Most form tools can't add that header on their own, so the easiest universal route is a no-code bridge like Zapier or Make.

zapier.title: Zapier or Make (works with any form — recommended)
zapier.body: Use your form as the trigger step (e.g. "New response in Google Forms"). Then add an action: in Zapier pick "Webhooks → POST", in Make pick "HTTP → Make a request". Set the URL above, method POST, add the header above, and map your form fields into the request body.

typeform.title: Typeform (direct)
typeform.body: In your form: Connect → Webhooks → Add a webhook, and paste the address above. Adding the Authorization header needs a paid Typeform plan; on a free plan, use the Zapier/Make route instead.

google.title: Google Forms
google.body: Easiest via Zapier/Make using the "New response" trigger. If you're comfortable: Extensions → Apps Script, and use UrlFetchApp to POST to the address above with the header.

squarespace.title: Squarespace / Wix
squarespace.body: These don't send webhooks on their own. Connect them through Zapier or Make (above) using their "new form submission" trigger.

recipes.note: Heads up: the address only works while the daemon is reachable at that host. When you go live, replace localhost with your public URL.

form.enable: Host a form for me (no website needed)
form.enableDesc: Turns on a ready-made web form anyone can fill in from a link — no Authorization header, no curl, no form tool required. Submissions run this flow.
form.fieldsDesc: Comma-separated field names. Leave blank for the default: name, email, message. A field called "message" becomes a large text box.

notifications.help: Get pinged when a run of this flow fails. The daemon POSTs a JSON payload to the webhook URL — works with Slack incoming-webhook URLs, Discord, Teams, PagerDuty events API, or any custom receiver.
notifications.webhookDesc: POSTed payload includes <0>graph_id</0>, <0>run_id</0>, <0>error_code</0>, <0>error_message</0>, <0>failed_node</0>, <0>run_url</0>. Leave blank to disable.

general.displayNameDesc: Friendly name shown in the flow list. Defaults to the ID.
general.iconPlaceholder: e.g. git, ntfy, claude, mail, globe, webhook
general.iconDesc: Logical icon name. Pick one of: git, ntfy, claude, mail, globe, webhook, sparkles, hammer, file-input, file-output, terminal, clock, database, cpu, workflow, git-branch, git-merge, repeat, timer, square-stack, user-check.
general.timeoutDesc: Auto-cancel the run if it hasn't finished by then. 0 / blank = no cap (the daemon's default still applies if one is set).
general.flowIdDesc: Changing the ID would orphan past runs; rename by creating a new flow and copying nodes.
general.orgVisibleDesc: Anyone in this workspace can see and run the flow. Only you (the owner) can edit it.
general.privateVisibleDesc: Only you (and tenant admins, for recovery) can see the flow. Triggers still fire it.
general.ownerDesc: Stamped by the daemon when the flow is first saved. Only tenant admins can transfer ownership.

connections.title: Your connections
connections.intro: Connect an app once here, then any flow you build can use it.
connections.firstTileBody: Most templates fire a notification or read a mailbox. Connecting Slack (for messages) and Google (for Gmail + Sheets) covers the majority of what you'll build first — pick the cards below and we'll guide you through the rest.
connections.setupIncompleteTitle: Setup isn't finished on this server yet
connections.setupIncompleteBody: Your administrator hasn't enabled the apps you can connect (Slack, Gmail, Notion, …) or the place where credentials get stored. Until that's done, there's nothing for you to do here — your flows that need those won't be able to run.
connections.setupIncompleteContactGeneric: Contact whoever set up this Hazy Flow workspace for you and ask them to finish the apps + credentials setup.

connections.credentialsIntro: Store a database URL, API key, or other secret a flow needs. Values are write-only — they're never shown again after you save.

connGate.title: Set up this flow first
connGate.lede: This flow uses apps or credentials you haven't set up yet. Add them so the run doesn't fail:
connGate.slackBody: Invite the Hazy Flow app to {{channels}} in Slack (open the channel, type /invite @Hazy Flow). Connecting Slack isn't enough on its own — the app also has to be a member of each channel it posts to, or the run fails.

connGate.adminBlockedBody: These aren't switched on in your Hazy Flow workspace yet. You can't enable them yourself — ask whoever set this up for you.
